title: Complexe de De Rham à puissance divisée [conférence de 1976 à l’IHÉS] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
This is not a manuscript page. It is a typed page, numbered '- 50 -' with the chapter mark 'IX' and the stamped number 368, filed among the handwritten De Rham notes. In content it matches the last part of §4.7 of SGA 7 I, Exposé IX (Grothendieck, 'Modèles de Néron et monodromie'). §4.7 is the rigidity lemma usually attributed to Serre (and going back to Minkowski).

The statement being proved: let G be a divisible commutative group object (e.g. an abelian variety, or its torsion or Tate module) and u an automorphism of finite order with u ≡ 1 mod n, i.e. u − 1 = n·v with v an endomorphism. Then u = 1 if n ≥ 3, and u² = 1 if n = 2.

Proof of 4.7.3 (end):
- The earlier part has reduced to u of p-power order p^N. The subring E generated by u, tensored with Q, is a quotient of Q[T]/(T^{p^N} − 1), which is a finite product of cyclotomic fields. Hence E_Q is a product of number fields K_i.
- Projecting E, u, v to each factor K_i reduces the claim to one statement. Let u be a primitive p^m-th root of unity in K = Q(u), and n ≥ 2 an integer with u − 1 ≡ 0 mod n in the ring of integers of K. Then u = 1, or u = −1 and n = 2.
- The key fact: for m ≥ 1, the ideal (u − 1) is prime and totally ramified, with (p) = (u − 1)^e, where e = φ(p^m). This exponent is > 1 except when p = 2 and m = 1, i.e. u = −1.
- If n divides u − 1, then (u − 1) ⊂ (n). Since (u − 1) is prime above p, this forces (n) = (u − 1). Hence n = p and e = 1, so u = −1 and n = 2.

4.7.4 (proof of 4.7.2): a group in which every element has square 1 is commutative, since xy = (xy)^{-1} = y^{-1}x^{-1} = yx. So Γ ≅ (Z/2)^r when it is finite.

Remark 4.7.5 combines the two. If a finite group Γ acts faithfully on a divisible commutative Group G of a topos and acts trivially on the n-torsion ₙG, then Γ = 1 for n ≥ 3, and Γ is an elementary abelian 2-group for n = 2. The topos formulation is a slight generalisation, typical of SGA 7.

Relation to the neighbouring pages: none mathematically. They concern Frobenius-type endomorphisms of divided-power differential bialgebras (Witt / crystalline context). This page appears to be a stray leaf, or reused paper from the typescript of SGA 7, included in the folder.
errors: Notation clash: the text says 'racine primitive p^n-ème' but then uses n as the modulus and m as the exponent ('u≠1 i.e. m≥1'). It should read p^m-th root of unity. Either the original typescript has a typo or the transcription misreads it.

Slightly elliptic step: 'n ≥ 2 ne peut diviser u−1 que si n=p'. Strictly, (u−1) ⊂ (n) with (u−1) prime gives (n) = (u−1). Then n is a power of p whose norm-type constraint forces n = p and e = 1. The conclusion is correct.

ideas.what: An automorphism of finite order of a divisible commutative group (abelian variety) that is ≡ 1 mod n is trivial for n ≥ 3, and an involution for n = 2. Proved via cyclotomic fields and ramification of (1 − ζ).
ideas.modern_name: Serre's rigidity lemma (Minkowski–Serre lemma); rigidity of level-n structures for n ≥ 3
ideas.usually_credited_to: Minkowski (for GL_n(Z)); J.-P. Serre (1960, 'Rigidité du foncteur de Jacobi d'échelon n ≥ 3')
ideas.where_published: SGA 7 I, Exposé IX, §4.7 (Lecture Notes in Math. 288)

ideas.what: A group of exponent 2 is commutative.
Formulation for a finite group acting faithfully on a divisible commutative Group of a topos, trivially on ₙG.

deep.surprise_reason: This is a typed page of the published SGA 7 Exposé IX (§4.7, Serre's lemma), stray among the De Rham notes. Its content is standard and published; it is of archival interest only as evidence of reuse of typescript paper.
transcription_corrections: 'racine primitive p^n-ème' should presumably be 'p^m-ème', consistent with the later 'm ≥ 1'.
The page is a typed sheet (SGA 7 IX, p. 50 of the exposé, overall stamp 368), not a manuscript page. The faint handwriting visible is bleed-through from the reverse side.
